model.rationale: Joyce pairs a ten-point Republican district lean with a massive fundraising advantage and no visible outside opposition against an underfunded challenger, while markets price his reelection near 94%. overview:
OH-14 is a Republican-held Northeast Ohio district with a ten-point Republican lean in its partisan fundamentals. David Joyce has held the seat since 2013 and is running again with the full advantages of incumbency. No public general-election polling exists for this race, and no national race raters have published ratings, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, campaign finance, and market pricing.

Joyce has raised about $1.4 million and holds $3.1 million on hand, while Democrat Maria Jukic has raised roughly $62,000 with $34,000 available, and no outside groups have engaged on either side. Prediction markets put the Republican's chances around 94%. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and a wide money gap points to a Republican hold, with the open question being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
